groups.name: Eko (Lagos Island and Mainland)
groups.description: Historic core of Lagos: the Eko settlement, seat of the Oba of Lagos and the Idejo (White Cap) chieftaincy, with Awori and returnee-descended communities.

ethnicMakeup.name: Aguda and Saro
ethnicMakeup.note: Afro-Brazilian and Sierra Leonean returnee descendants

groups.name: Awori
groups.description: Awori Yoruba sub-group of Lagos and south-western Ogun, indigenous to much of the Lagos mainland and Ota.

groups.name: Egun (Badagry)
groups.description: Egun (Gun/Ogu) coastal people of Badagry, a community that continues across the border into Benin Republic; Badagry was a major slave-trade port.

wikiNotes.title: Egun (Badagry)
wikiNotes.note: Home of the Egun Zangbeto night-guardian masquerades.

groups.name: Lagos Ijebu (Ikorodu, Epe, Ibeju-Lekki)
groups.description: Ijebu-related lagoon-side communities in the eastern non-metropolitan part of Lagos State; Awori communities are also present in Ibeju-Lekki.

groups.name: Oyo (Alaafin's Kingdom)
groups.description: Heartland of the historic Oyo Empire around present-day Oyo town, seat of the Alaafin of Oyo.

groups.name: Oke-Ogun
groups.description: The savanna plain of north-western Oyo State, home to Oyo-Yoruba communities such as Saki, Igboho and Iseyin, the last known for Aso-Oke weaving.

groups.name: Ibarapa
groups.description: The Ibarapa Yoruba towns (Igboora, Igangan, Tapa and neighbours) on the western edge of Oyo State.

groups.name: Iwo-Ede-Ejigbo axis
groups.description: Oyo-Yoruba towns of north-western Osun State, including the seats of the Oluwo of Iwo, the Timi of Ede and the Olojigbo of Ejigbo.

groups.name: Akoko
groups.description: Hill-country Yoruba sub-group of north-eastern Ondo State organised in many small kingdoms (Ikare, Oka, Ikaram and others).

wikiNotes.title: Akoko
wikiNotes.note: Hosts the Ariginya (local wrestling) festival at Ikare-Akoko.

groups.name: Ilaje
groups.description: Riverine and coastal Yoruba sub-group of southern Ondo State, fishing and oil-region communities of the Atlantic coast.

wikiNotes.title: Ilaje
wikiNotes.note: Shares the Biripo musical tradition with the Apoi and the Ikale.

groups.name: Ikale
groups.description: Yoruba sub-group of southern Ondo State centred on Okitipupa and Irele, in Ikaleland.

wikiNotes.title: Ikale
wikiNotes.note: Shares the Biripo musical tradition with the Ilaje and Apoi; also known for the Irokute festival at Okitipupa.

groups.name: Ondo Kingdom and neighbours
groups.description: Yoruba communities around the Ondo Kingdom under the Osemawe of Ondo and Ile-Oluji.

groups.name: Ekiti Yoruba
groups.description: The whole of Ekiti State, homeland of the Ekiti sub-group of the Yoruba, organised in some sixteen historic kingdoms each with its own crowned Oba.

groups.name: Igbomina and Ekiti (Kwara)
groups.description: Igbomina and Ekiti-Yoruba communities of southern Kwara State.

groups.name: Nupe (Kwara)
groups.description: Nupe communities along the Niger River in northern Kwara State, seat of the Etsu Patigi.

groups.name: Baruba (Borgu, Kwara)
groups.description: Baruba (Bariba/Baatonu) and related Borgu communities in the north-west of Kwara State, continuous with the Borgu region of Benin Republic.

groups.name: FCT indigenous peoples
groups.description: The original inhabitants of the Federal Capital Territory, who lived in the area long before Abuja was built.

wikiNotes.title: FCT indigenous peoples
wikiNotes.note: Indigenous groups are recognised through area-council traditional rulers such as the Ona of Abaji.

groups.name: Berom
groups.description: Largest indigenous people of the Jos Plateau, centred on Jos South, Barkin Ladi and Riyom under the Gbong Gwom Jos.

wikiNotes.title: Berom
wikiNotes.note: Their festivals were merged into the annual Nzem Berom cultural festival held around April.

groups.name: Ngas and Mwaghavul (central Plateau)
groups.description: Ngas (Pankshin, Kanke) and Mwaghavul (Mangu, Bokkos) communities of the central Plateau highlands.

groups.name: Southern Plateau (Tarok, Goemai, Pan, Mupun)
groups.description: Tarok (Langtang), Goemai (Shendam), Pan (Qua'an Pan) and related communities of the southern Plateau lowlands.

groups.name: Igala
groups.description: Eastern Kogi kingdom centred on Idah, seat of the Attah Igala.

wikiNotes.title: Igala
wikiNotes.note: Idah hosts the Ocho hunting festival, banned in 1963 and revived in 2018.

groups.name: Ebira
groups.description: Ebira (Igbira) heartland of central Kogi around Okene, under the Ohinoyi of Ebiraland; Ogori and Magongo communities have distinct local traditions.

groups.name: Okun Yoruba
groups.description: Yoruba-speaking Okun communities (Kabba, Ijumu, Yagba, Mopa) of western Kogi.

ethnicMakeup.name: Okun Yoruba (Owe, Bunu, Yagba, Ijumu, Iyagba)

groups.name: Tiv
groups.description: Tiv heartland of Benue State under the Tor Tiv; the Tiv also live in Nasarawa, Taraba and Plateau states.

wikiNotes.title: Tiv
wikiNotes.note: Home of the Kwagh-hir theatrical tradition, inscribed by UNESCO in 2019.

groups.name: Idoma
groups.description: Idoma communities of southern Benue State around Otukpo, seat of the Och'Idoma.

wikiNotes.title: Idoma
wikiNotes.note: Home of the Eje Alekwu ancestral festival.

groups.name: Igede
groups.description: Igede-speaking communities of Oju and Obi in south-eastern Benue State.

wikiNotes.title: Igede
wikiNotes.note: Known for the Ige-Agba new yam festival.

groups.name: Eggon
groups.description: Eggon communities of northern Nasarawa State, under the Aren Eggon.

groups.name: Alago (Arago) and neighbours
groups.description: Alago, Migili and related communities of southern Nasarawa State, including the Doma chiefdom under the Osana of Doma.

groups.name: Nupe (Niger State)
groups.description: Nupe kingdom of central Niger State centred on Bida, seat of the Etsu Nupe.

wikiNotes.title: Nupe (Niger State)
wikiNotes.note: Bida is known for brasswork and glass-bead making.

groups.name: Gbagyi (Gwari) of Niger State
groups.description: Gbagyi (Gwari) communities of eastern Niger State, including the Minna area.

groups.name: Borgu and Kambari
groups.description: Kambari, Bokobaru and other communities of north-western Niger State along the Benin Republic border.

groups.name: Southern Kaduna peoples
groups.description: The highland peoples of southern Kaduna State, including Kataf (Atyap), Bajju, Ham (Jaba), Kagoro (Gworok), Fantswam, Ikulu, Adara and Kurama.

wikiNotes.title: Southern Kaduna peoples
wikiNotes.note: The Nok terracotta culture is named after Nok village in Jaba LGA; the Afan festival is held at Kagoro on 1 January.

groups.name: Daura Emirate
groups.description: Hausa communities of northern Katsina State around Daura, regarded in tradition as the ancestral home of the Hausa.

wikiNotes.title: Daura Emirate
wikiNotes.note: Daura is tied to the Bayajidda legend of Hausa origins.

groups.name: Zuru (Dakarkari)
groups.description: The Dakarkari and related peoples of the Zuru Emirate in southern Kebbi State.

groups.name: Yauri Emirate
groups.description: The Yauri Emirate on the Niger River in south-western Kebbi State, home of the Reshe, Gungawa and related river peoples.

groups.name: Argungu (Kebbawa)
groups.description: The Kebbawa communities of the Argungu Emirate, historic heart of the Kebbi Kingdom.

wikiNotes.title: Argungu (Kebbawa)
wikiNotes.note: Host of the Argungu Fishing Festival.

groups.name: Hadejia Emirate
groups.description: Hausa communities of the Hadejia Emirate on the Hadejia-Jama'are floodplain of Jigawa State.

groups.name: Kanuri heartland
groups.description: Core Kanuri-speaking LGAs of Borno State, successors of the Kanem-Bornu Empire and the Shehu of Borno's domain.

groups.name: Bura (Babur) and Biu
groups.description: The Bura (Babur) and related communities of the Biu plateau in southern Borno State, under the Mai of Biu.

groups.name: Marghi, Kibaku and Gwoza hill peoples
groups.description: Marghi, Kibaku (Chibok) and Gwoza hill peoples of southern Borno State.

groups.name: Bachama (Bwatiye)
groups.description: Bachama (Bwatiye) communities of the Benue valley in southern Adamawa State, under the Hama Bachama.

groups.name: Northern Adamawa highland peoples
groups.description: Kamwe (Higi), Kilba, Fali, Margi and neighbouring peoples of the Mandara-foothill north of Adamawa State.

wikiNotes.title: Northern Adamawa highland peoples
wikiNotes.note: The Sukur Cultural Landscape lies in Madagali LGA.

groups.name: Jukun (Wukari Federation)
groups.description: Jukun communities of southern Taraba State under the Aku Uka of Wukari, successors of the Kwararafa confederacy.

wikiNotes.title: Jukun (Wukari Federation)
wikiNotes.note: Ibi hosts the Nwonyo International Fishing and Cultural Festival.

groups.name: Kuteb and Ichen (Takum)
groups.description: Kuteb, Ichen and related communities of Takum and Ussa in south-eastern Taraba State.

groups.name: Mumuye
groups.description: Mumuye communities of central Taraba State, renowned for their figurative wood sculpture.

groups.name: Mambilla
groups.description: Mambilla Plateau communities of Taraba State along the Cameroon border.

groups.name: Sayawa (Zaar)
groups.description: Sayawa (Zaar) communities of southern Bauchi State.

groups.name: Tangale and Waja
groups.description: Tangale (Billiri, Kaltungo) and Waja (Balanga, Shongom) communities of southern Gombe State.

groups.name: Fika Emirate
groups.description: The Fika Emirate of southern Yobe State, under the Mai of Fika, home of the Bolewa, Ngizim and Karekare.

groups.name: Ohafia, Arochukwu and Abam
groups.description: Igbo communities of north-eastern Abia State: the Aro of Arochukwu, the Ohafia warrior tradition and the Abam.

groups.name: Ngwa and Ukwa
groups.description: Ngwa and Ukwa Igbo communities of southern Abia State, hinterland of the Aba commercial centre.

groups.name: Ibeku and Umuahia axis
groups.description: Igbo communities of central and northern Abia around Umuahia (Ibeku), including Ikwuano and Isuikwuato.

groups.name: Mbaise
groups.description: The three Mbaise LGAs of Imo State, a densely populated Igbo cultural area.

groups.name: Orlu area
groups.description: Igbo communities of the Orlu area of Imo State, including Nkwerre and Ideato, home of Arondizuogu.

wikiNotes.title: Orlu area
wikiNotes.note: Arondizuogu in Ideato North hosts the Ikeji masquerade festival.

groups.name: Okigwe area
groups.description: Igbo communities of northern Imo State around Okigwe.

groups.name: Oguta and Egbema
groups.description: Igbo communities of the Oguta Lake area and the Egbema oil belt in south-western Imo State.

groups.name: Nri-Awka heartland
groups.description: The Nri and Awka heartland of Anambra State, associated with the ritual Nri Kingdom and Awka's metalworking tradition.

wikiNotes.title: Nri-Awka heartland
wikiNotes.note: The Eze Nri holds a ritual kingship associated with the Nri Kingdom.

groups.name: Anambra River basin
groups.description: River-basin communities of northern Anambra State, including Aguleri and Umueri; Anambra West has strong Igala links.

groups.name: Nnewi, Aguata and Orumba
groups.description: Igbo communities of southern Anambra State, home of Nnewi's industrial cluster.

groups.name: Nsukka Igbo
groups.description: The Igbo communities of northern Enugu State, centred on Nsukka.

groups.name: Nkanu
groups.description: Nkanu Igbo communities south of Enugu.

groups.name: Udi, Awgu and Oji River area
groups.description: Igbo communities of the western Enugu escarpment, including the Ngwo clan associated with the Odo festival.

ethnicMakeup.name: Igbo (Udi, Awgu, Ezeagu, Oji River, Aninri)

groups.name: Afikpo (Ehugbo)
groups.description: The Afikpo (Ehugbo) Igbo of southern Ebonyi State, known for elaborate masquerade traditions.

groups.name: Ezza, Izzi and Ikwo
groups.description: Northern Ebonyi Igbo communities around Abakaliki, including Izzi, Ezza and Ikwo.

groups.name: Ivo, Ohaozara and Onicha
groups.description: Igbo communities of south-western Ebonyi State, including the Uburu and Okposi salt-lake areas.

groups.name: Ikwerre
groups.description: Ikwerre communities, indigenous to Port Harcourt and Obio-Akpor and to the Ikwerre and Emohua areas.

groups.name: Ogoni
groups.description: The four Ogoni-linked LGAs of south-eastern Rivers State.

ethnicMakeup.name: Eleme
ethnicMakeup.note: Distinct language, usually counted with Ogoniland

groups.name: Eastern Ijaw and Degema (Kalabari, Okrika, Bonny, Opobo)
groups.description: Eastern Ijaw kingdoms of the Rivers creeks, including Kalabari, Okrika, Bonny and Opobo, plus the Degema.

wikiNotes.title: Eastern Ijaw and Degema (Kalabari, Okrika, Bonny, Opobo)
wikiNotes.note: The Ekine (Sekiapu) masquerade society is central to Kalabari culture.

groups.name: Etche, Ekpeye, Ogba and Omuma
groups.description: Igbo-related communities of northern and central Rivers State.

groups.name: Obolo (Andoni)
groups.description: Obolo (Andoni) communities across the Rivers/Akwa Ibom coast.

groups.name: Ijaw of Bayelsa
groups.description: The Ijaw (Izon) clans of Bayelsa State, with Epie-Atissa in Yenagoa.

wikiNotes.title: Ijaw of Bayelsa
wikiNotes.note: Nembe (Brass) was a major palm-oil trading kingdom.

groups.name: Ogbia
groups.description: The Ogbia people of Bayelsa State, in whose area Oloibiri lies.

wikiNotes.title: Ogbia
wikiNotes.note: Oloibiri saw Nigeria's first commercial oil discovery in 1956.

groups.name: Ibibio
groups.description: Ibibio communities, the largest group in Akwa Ibom State.

groups.name: Annang
groups.description: Annang communities of north-western Akwa Ibom State, closely related to the Ibibio.

groups.name: Oron
groups.description: Oron communities of the south-eastern Akwa Ibom coast.

groups.name: Eket and Ibeno
groups.description: Eket and Ibeno communities of the south-western Akwa Ibom coast and its oil-industry belt.

groups.name: Efik and Calabar area
groups.description: Efik and related communities of the Calabar estuary, an Atlantic trading society governed through the Ekpe society.

groups.name: Ekoi (Ejagham)
groups.description: Ekoi (Ejagham) communities of the central Cross River forest belt, including the Ikom monolith area.

groups.name: Yakurr, Abi and Biase
groups.description: Yakö (Yakurr), Abi and Biase communities of southern-central Cross River State.

wikiNotes.title: Yakurr, Abi and Biase
wikiNotes.note: Ugep in Yakurr hosts the Leboku new yam festival.

groups.name: Northern Cross River (Ogoja, Bekwarra, Boki, Yala, Obudu)
groups.description: Boki, Bekwarra, Yala, Bette and Ogoja communities of northern Cross River State.

groups.name: Itsekiri
groups.description: The Itsekiri Kingdom of the western Niger Delta under the Olu of Warri, with Ode-Itsekiri as its cradle.

ethnicMakeup.name: Ijaw and Urhobo
ethnicMakeup.note: Mixed communities; local claims are contested

wikiNotes.title: Itsekiri
wikiNotes.note: Itsekiri identity centres on the Olu of Warri, who marks his coronation anniversary each August.

groups.name: Urhobo
groups.description: Urhobo kingdoms of the central Delta State.

ethnicMakeup.name: Okpe
ethnicMakeup.note: Closely related to Urhobo, with its own traditional ruler

groups.name: Isoko
groups.description: Isoko communities of southern Delta State.

groups.name: Ijaw of Delta
groups.description: Ijaw communities of the Delta creeks, including the Gbaramatu Kingdom in Warri South West.

wikiNotes.title: Ijaw of Delta
wikiNotes.note: Gbaramatu Kingdom hosts the seven-day Amaseikumor festival.

groups.name: Anioma (Delta Igbo)
groups.description: Igbo-speaking communities of Delta North, often grouped as Anioma, west of the Niger.

groups.name: Ukwuani (Kwale)
groups.description: The Ukwuani (Kwale) people of southern Delta North, whose language is close to but distinct from Igbo.

groups.name: Edo (Bini) heartland
groups.description: Edo (Bini) heartland of southern Edo State, home of the Benin Kingdom and its Oba.

groups.name: Esan
groups.description: Esan communities of central Edo State, whose rulers bear the title Onojie.

groups.name: Afemai (Etsako, Owan and Akoko-Edo)
groups.description: The northern Edo peoples, called Afemai, including Etsako, Owan and Akoko-Edo communities.

ethnicMakeup.name: Akoko-Edo
ethnicMakeup.note: Distinct Edoid-speaking communities, not to be confused with Akoko in Ondo State
